correctness.rationale: The normalized S³ addition theorem gives the dense sample Gram kernel (1/120)Σ(n+1)U_n(x·y). I inspected the exact class-algebra certificate and independently reconstructed the matrices from the vertices using dense integer-pair arithmetic in Z[φ], without assuming class closure. The annihilators and trace moments give ranks 1,5,14,30,55,91,116,120; at L=7 the eigenvalues 0,1,7/4,7/3 have multiplicities 4,91,16,9, and at L=8 the eigenvalues 1,7/4,7/3,4 have multiplicities 55,16,45,4. These are cumulative cutoffs. The check also gives B1=1 and a constant top-eigenspace projector diagonal 1/30. Thus, if the positive weights have mean 1, the mean Rayleigh quotient in the top eigenspace of B^(1/2)WB^(1/2) is 4 and the quotient on the constant vector is 1. Equality of the condition number with 2 forces the constant vector to be a minimum eigenvector; invertibility of B^(1/2) forces W1=1. This proves rigidity, independently of the stated symmetry-averaging argument. The inverse polynomial agrees with the reciprocal at all four eigenvalues, and R*B^(-1) is the minimum-L²-norm right inverse.
residual_risks: The matrix certificate is finite and proves no statement at higher cutoffs or for other point sets. The full-row-rank condition number uses the smallest nonzero singular value.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the quantitative 600-cell interpolation theorem with rigidity of its optimal positive weighting at the first surjective cutoff. The spectral component alone is derivable from classical character convolution and the affine E8 tensoring rule; it is not credited as a new decomposition. Later exact-degree records directly imply the cumulative spectra but not the positive-weight equality characterization, and neither establishes earlier priority. The inspected earlier harmonic mode and design literature does not supply the combined theorem. The uniqueness step uses standard eigenvalue bounds but also requires the specific bottom-eigenvector geometry and an equality argument.
residual_risks: An earlier result on diagonal-rescaling rigidity might subsume the weighted result; exact theorem text for the named optimization paper was not available.
A pre-existing 600-cell association-scheme table could furnish another direct derivation of the numerical spectrum; that portion is not independently credited as original.

value.rationale: For this canonical spherical point set the first cutoff at which arbitrary data interpolate is a natural stability threshold. The weighted theorem excludes every positive diagonal reweighting as an improvement, even allowing equality only for constant weights. Together with the explicit right inverse and sharp norm it gives a concrete prescription at that threshold, not merely a recomputation of a character table.
